(p. 595)

**Surah "al-Nazi'at" (The Pluckers)**

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

﴿By those who pull out with violence﴾, ﴿and those who extract gently﴾, ﴿and those who glide swiftly﴾, ﴿then those who race ahead﴾, ﴿then those who arrange affairs﴾. There is no pause (waqf) here; rather, a required pause (lazim) is observed here, because if one continued reading, "yawma" (on the day) would become a time-adverb (zarf) of "al-mudabbirat" (those who arrange), and the arranging of the angels has ended on that day.

He, glorified is He, swore by groups of angels who pull souls out of bodies with violence (gharq), meaning: with extreme force in the pulling out. That is, they pull them from the extremities of the bodies, from the fingertips and the places of the nails. And by the groups that extract them, meaning: bring them out, from the expression "nashata al-dalw min al-bi'r" (he drew the bucket out of the well), when he pulled it out. And by the groups that glide in their passage, meaning: that hasten, so they race ahead to what they have been commanded, and thus arrange a matter among the affairs of the servants, of what sets right their religion or their worldly life, as has been decreed for them.

Or [the oaths are sworn] by the horses of warriors which pull hard at their bridles, so that the bridles are drawn taut because of the length of their necks, since they are purebred (ʿirab) horses. And [by those] that leave the abode of Islam for the abode of war, from your saying "thawrun nashitun" (an agitated bull), when it leaves one land for another. And [by those] that glide in their running, so they race ahead to the goal, and thus arrange the matter of victory and triumph. The attribution of the arranging to them is because they are among its causes.

Or [the oaths are sworn] by the stars which travel from the east to the west, and their "ighraq" in the pulling out is that they cross the whole sphere until they descend at the farthest west. And [by those] that move from one zodiacal sign (burj) to another, and [by those] that glide in the orbit (falak) among the wandering planets (sayyarah), so they race ahead and thus arrange a matter from the science of calculation (ʿilm al-hisab).

The answer to the oath is omitted, and it is "la-tub'athunna" (you will surely be resurrected), because what follows it indicates it, namely the mention of the Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 79, verse 6:

﴿On the Day when the quaker quakes﴾, it moves with a violent motion; and "al-rajf" (ar-rajf): the intensity of motion.

﴿The quaker﴾ (al-Raajifah): the first blast (al-nafkhah al-ula). It is described by what occurs upon its happening, because the earth is convulsed by it until everyone upon it dies.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 79, verse 7:

﴿Tatba'uha﴾, a circumstantial clause (hal) referring to "al-Raajifa" (the Quake),

﴿al-Radifa﴾: the second blast (al-nafkha al-thaniya), so called because it follows (tardufu) the first. Between them is a span of forty years. The first blast causes the creation to die, and the second brings them back to life.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 79, verse 8:

﴿Hearts on that Day﴾: the hearts of those who deny the Resurrection (al-ba'th).

﴿Will be trembling﴾: agitated, anxious, from "al-wajif" (trembling, palpitation), which is "al-wajib" (throbbing). The accusative of "Yawma tarjuf" (the Day when the earth quakes) is governed by what is indicated by "Hearts on that Day will be trembling," meaning: on the Day when the earth quakes, the hearts will tremble. The nominative of "Hearts" is by way of the inchoative (mubtada'), and "trembling" is its attribute (sifah).

Their eyes ﴿will be downcast﴾, that is, the eyes of their owners,

﴿humbled﴾, abased, from the terror of what they behold. Its predicate is:

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 79, verse 10:

﴿They say﴾: that is, those who deny the Resurrection in this world, mocking and rejecting the Resurrection,

﴿"Shall we indeed be returned to our former state?"﴾ The interrogative here carries the meaning of denial: that is, "Shall we be returned after our death to the first state, so that we come back alive as we were?" Al-ḥāfira (the former state) means the original condition. It is said of one who was in a matter, then left it, and then returned to it: "He returned to his ḥāfira," meaning to his original condition. It is also said: "The payment is at the ḥāfira," meaning at the original condition, which is the (first) transaction. They denied the Resurrection, then increased their disbelief by declaring it far-fetched, and said:

﴿Shall we indeed, when we are bones, decayed?﴾ Meaning: worn away, and rotted (نَاخِرَةً). The Kufan readers other than Hafs read it as **ناخِرَةً** (*nākhira*). The form **نَخِرَةً** (*nakhira*, pattern *fa'il*, an intensive form) is more emphatic than **فاعِلٌ** (*fā'il*, the active participle pattern). It is said: "the bone decayed (نَخِرَ الْعَظْمُ), so it is *nakhir* and *nākhir*." The meaning is: Shall we be returned to life after we have become worn-out bones? The word **إذا** (*idhā*, "when") is in the accusative, governed by a deleted verb, which is **نُبْعَثُ** (we will be raised).

Translation:

﴿They say﴾: that is, those who deny the Resurrection,

﴿That﴾, our return,

﴿would then be a losing return﴾: a return bringing loss, or its people would be losers. The meaning is: if it is true, and we are raised up, then we would be losers, because of our denial of it. This is said by them in mockery.

Quranic quotations keep ﴿﴾ markers. Page marker (p-٥٩٧) is presumably a page reference; I'll keep it as it appears since it's part of the text.

(p-597) ﴿Then it will be but a single shout﴾. It is connected to an omitted element, meaning: do not consider that return difficult for God, Mighty and Majestic; rather it is easy and simple in His power. So it is but a single cry, meaning the second blast (al-nafkha al-thaniya), from the expression "zajara al-ba'ir" (he drove the camel with a shout), when one shouts at it.

Then, behold, they will be upon the surface of the earth, alive, after having been dead in its belly. It has also been said that "al-Sahirah" is a specific land in Syria, beside Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), or the land of Makkah, or Jahannam (Hell).

Qur'anic quotation: ﴿Has the story of Musa reached you?﴾ This is an interrogative (istifham) which contains an alert (tanbih) to the fact that this is among the matters that must be attended to, and an honouring (tashrif) of the one addressed by it.

﴿When his Lord called to him﴾ — when He called to him,

﴿in the sacred valley, Tuwa﴾ — the blessed and purified (valley),

﴿Tuwa﴾ — its name.

Go to Pharaoh, for he has transgressed, (meaning: the verse is to be read with an implied "say"),

Let me correct that and translate it properly:

﴿Go to Pharaoh﴾, with the implied sense of "saying" (ʿalā irādat al-qawl), that is, the phrase is understood as "[saying:] Go to Pharaoh";

﴿Indeed he has transgressed﴾, he went beyond the limit in disbelief and corruption.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 79, verse 18:

﴿So say: "Do you have any inclination to purify yourself?"﴾ Do you have any inclination to purify yourself (tatahhara) from polytheism (shirk) and disobedience (i'syan), through obedience (ta'ah) and faith (iman)? And [the reading of] with the doubling of the zay (tashdid al-zay) is that of the Hijazi [reciters].

﴿وَأهْدِيَكَ إلى رَبِّكَ﴾: and I will guide you to your Lord. And I will guide you to the knowledge of God by mentioning His attributes, so that you know Him,

﴿فَتَخْشى﴾: so that you fear Him, because fear (khashya) exists only with knowledge. God, may He be exalted, said: ﴿إنَّما يَخْشى اللهَ مِن عِبادِهِ العُلَماءُ﴾ [Fatir: 28]: Only those among His servants who have knowledge fear God, i.e., those who know Him. It is related from some of the sages: "Know God, for whoever knows God cannot disobey Him even for the blink of an eye." So fear is the essence of the matter: whoever fears God does all good, and whoever feels secure becomes bold in every evil. From this is the hadith: "Whoever fears sets out at night, and whoever sets out at night reaches the destination."

[God] began His address to him with a question, whose meaning is an offer, as a man says to his guest: "Would you like to stay with us?" He followed it with gentle speech, to invite him with kindness in speech, and to bring him down from his arrogance through conciliation, as He commanded in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿فَقُولا لَهُ قَوْلا لَيِّنًا﴾ [Ta-Ha: 44]: Speak to him with gentle speech.
﴿So he showed him the greatest sign﴾. That is: he went and showed Pharaoh the staff, or the staff and the white hand, since the two are in the ruling of one sign.

﴿So he denied﴾, Pharaoh denied Moses and the great sign, and called them "a sorcerer" and "sorcery",

﴿and disobeyed﴾, God (exalted is He).

Then he turned his back, (ﷺ) —

Actually, I must render this precisely without the stray honorific; here is the translation:

﴿Then he turned his back﴾, he turned away from Musa (Moses),

﴿striving﴾, he exerted himself in plotting against him; or, when he saw the serpent he turned his back in terror, hastening in his walk, and he was hasty and light-headed (ṭayyāsh, khafīf).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 79, verse 23:

﴿Then he gathered [his people]﴾: he gathered the sorcerers and his soldiers.

﴿And proclaimed﴾: in the place where they had assembled with him.
﴿So he said, "I am your lord, the most high."﴾ "There is no lord above me." They had idols that they worshipped.

Then Allah seized him with the punishment of the Hereafter and the first (punishment). Al-Nasafi's commentary on this verse:

﴿So Allah seized him with the punishment of the Hereafter﴾: Allah punished him with the punishment of the Hereafter. "Al-nakal" (exemplary punishment) is in the sense of "al-tankil" (making an example of someone), like "al-salam" (greeting) in the sense of "al-taslim" (the act of greeting). Its being in the accusative is as a verbal noun (maf'ul mutlaq), because "akhadha" (seized) here carries the sense of "nakkala" (made an example of), as if it were said: "Allah made an example of him with the exemplary punishment of the Hereafter," that is, the burning (al-ihraq).

﴿And the first﴾: that is, the drowning (al-ighraq). Or, the exemplary punishment of his two statements: the last, which is "I am your Lord, the Most High" (Qur'an 79:24), and the first, which is "I know of no god for you other than myself" (Qur'an 28:38). Between them were forty years, or thirty, or twenty.

﴿Indeed in that﴾, the aforementioned,

﴿is a lesson for whoever fears﴾, Allah.

"Are you" (addressing you, O deniers of the Resurrection), "harder to create" (more difficult in creation and origination), "or the heaven?" It is a mubtada' (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, meaning: "Or the heaven, is it harder to create?" The commentator then explains how He created it, saying: "He built it," meaning Allah. Then he explained the building, saying:

[Qur'anic quotation] "He raised its canopy high"—he made its height (samk) elevated: he raised its ceiling. It was said: He made the extent of its ascent in the direction of height lofty, a journey of five hundred years.

"And He leveled it"—He made it even and balanced, without cracks or fissures.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 79, verse 29:

﴿And He darkened its night﴾, He made it dark.

﴿And brought forth its forenoon﴾, He brought out the light of its sun. The night and the sun are attributed to the heaven (al-sama'), because the night is its darkness and the sun is its lamp.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 79, verse 30:

﴿And the earth, after that He spread it out (dahaha)﴾: he spread it out (basatha). It had been created not spread out (madhuwwa), so it was spread out (fa-duhiyat) from Makkah, two thousand years after the creation of the heaven. Then he explained the spreading out (al-bast), saying:

﴿He brought forth from it its water﴾, by making the springs gush forth,

﴿and its pasture﴾, its herbage. For this reason the conjunction (*al-ʿāṭif*) does not precede "*akhraja*" [the second], or "*akhraja*" is a circumstantial clause (*ḥāl*), with "*wa-qad*" implied.

﴿And the mountains—He set them firm﴾: "arsaha" means He established them and made them firm.

The words "الْأَرْضَ" (al-ard, "the earth") and "الْجِبَالَ" (al-jibal, "the mountains") are in the accusative case (nasb) because of an implied verb: "dahaha" (He spread it out) and "arsa" (He set it firm), in accordance with the condition of tafsir (shart al-tafsir, the grammatical rule that the implied verb must be of the same kind as the verb that explains it).
﴿as a provision for you and for your cattle﴾. He did that as a provision for you and for your livestock.

Verse 34 of Surah al-Nazi'at (79): "But when the Great Calamity (al-Ṭāmmah al-Kubrā) comes."

The Great Calamity: the great disaster (al-Dāhiyah al-ʿUẓmā), which overwhelms (taṭimm ʿalā) the other calamities (al-dawāhī), meaning it rises above them and prevails over them. It is the Second Blast (al-nafkhah al-thāniyah), or the Hour in which the people of Paradise are driven to Paradise and the people of the Fire are driven to the Fire.

﴿On the day when man will remember﴾ is a *badal* (substitute, or appositive) for "إذا جاءَتْ" (*idha ja'at*, "when it comes"). That is, when he sees his deeds recorded in his book, he will remember them, though he had forgotten them.

﴿what he strove for﴾: "ما" (*ma*) is either *masdariyyah* (verbal, forming a verbal noun), meaning "his striving," or *mawsulah* (relative), meaning "that which he strove for."

And Hell is made manifest (﴿وَبُرِّزَتِ الجَحِيمُ﴾), meaning it is brought forth and displayed,

for whoever sees (﴿لِمَن يَرى﴾), meaning for every beholder, since its manifestation is a clear manifestation.

Translation:

﴿Then as for﴾ is the answer to "then when" (fa-idha): that is, when the Overwhelming Calamity comes, the matter is indeed as follows,

﴿whoever transgressed﴾: exceeded the limit, and so disbelieved.
[Qur'an 79:38] "And preferred the worldly life" over the Hereafter, by following the desires.

﴿Indeed, Hellfire is the refuge﴾: its refuge (مَأْواهُ). The alif and lam (ال) are a substitute for the possessive construction (al-idafa, the genitive construction). This is the view of the Kufans, of Sibawayh, and of the Basrans, who say: "it is the refuge for him" (هِيَ المَأْوى لَهُ).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 79, verse 40:

﴿And as for him who feared the standing before his Lord﴾, i.e., he knew that there is a standing for him on the Day of Resurrection before the reckoning of his Lord,

﴿and restrained the soul﴾, the one that commands to evil,

﴿from desire﴾, the destructive one, i.e., he restrained it from following its appetites. It is also said: this is the man who is inclined to disobedience, then remembers his standing for the reckoning, and so abandons it. (p-600) And "al-hawa" (desire): the inclination of the soul toward its appetites.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 79, verse 41:

﴿Indeed, Paradise is the refuge.﴾ That is: the place of return.
﴿They ask you about the Hour: when is its appointed time?﴾ When is its *irsa'* (إرْساؤُها)? That is, its *iqamah* (إقامَتُها), meaning: when will God (Exalted is He) establish it and make it firm?

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 79, verse 43:

﴿Why are you (concerned) with mentioning it?﴾ In what matter are you with regard to mentioning its time to them and informing them of it? That is: you are not (in any position) to mention it to them and to specify its time, in any matter, like your saying: "So-and-so has no share of knowledge in anything" (laysa fulanun mina al-'ilmi fi shay'). «The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) kept on mentioning the Hour and asking about it until this was revealed.» So, according to this, it is an expression of wonder at the frequency of his mentioning it; that is: they ask you about it, and out of your eagerness for answering them you keep on mentioning it and asking about it.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 79, verse 44:

﴿إلى رَبِّكَ مُنْتَهاها﴾: "its end (muntaha) is the knowledge of when it will occur, which belongs to none but Him." Or, "fīma" (why/for what) is a denial of their asking about it, i.e., "Why is this question being asked?" Then He said: "You are of its remembrance (min dhikrāhā)," i.e., your being sent, and you are the last of the prophets, a sign among its signs. So there is no sense in their asking about it. It is not far-fetched that this be stopped at "fīma." It was also said: "You are of its remembrance" is connected to the question, i.e., ﴿They ask you about the Hour, when will it arrive?﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 42], and [they say]: "Where are you in its remembrance?!" Then he resumed, saying: "﴿To your Lord is its finality﴾."

﴿Innama anta munthiru man yakhshaha﴾ (You are only a warner to those who fear it). Meaning: you were not sent to inform them of the time of the Hour. Rather, you were sent to warn of its terrors those who fear its severities.

"Munthirun" (مُنْذِرٌ), with tanwin (nunation, مُنَوَّنٌ), is the reading of Yazid and ʿAyyash.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 79, verse 46:

﴿As if they, on the day they see it﴾ — i.e., the Hour —

﴿they had not remained﴾ — in the worldly life —

﴿except for an evening or its morning﴾ — i.e., the morning of the evening. They considered the duration of their stay in the world to be small because of what they witnessed of the terror, like His saying: ﴿They will feel as if they had not remained except an hour of a day﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 35], and His saying: ﴿They will say, "We remained a day or part of a day"﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 113]. The attribution of ad-duha (the morning, forenoon) to al-ashiyya (the evening) is valid because of the close connection (mula-basa) between them, through their both being within one day. The meaning is that the duration of their stay did not reach a full day, but rather one of the two ends of the day: its evening, or its morning.
